pi.name: Laura Buttitta
pi.title: Professor of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology
pi.bio: Laura Buttitta earned her Ph.D. from Johns Hopkins University in 2004 and completed postdoctoral training with Bruce Edgar at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center. She opened her lab in the Department of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology at the University of Michigan in January 2011. Her research focuses on how the cell cycle is shut off in quiescent cells, such as differentiated or stem cells, using Drosophila and mammalian systems. She teaches MCDB 440, Cell Cycle Control and Cancer.

description: The Buttitta Lab studies states of G0 in development, cancer, and aging: how the cell cycle machinery is controlled during the decision to exit the cell cycle, and how quiescence is made reversible or irreversible in different biological contexts. The lab uses Drosophila melanogaster genetics together with mammalian cell lines to dissect the signals, phosphatases, and chromatin changes that enforce cell cycle exit. Projects range from the PP2A-B56 phosphatase complex and tumor dormancy in prostate cancer, to chromatin-mediated silencing of cell cycle genes in postmitotic tissues, hormone-driven quiescence and polyploid cell cycles in the fly accessory gland, and abnormal cell cycle re-entry in the aging brain. The work has applications to tissue regeneration, aging, and cancer.

areas.title: Modulators of the proliferation-quiescence decision
areas.summary: Studies how the PP2A phosphatase complex, particularly the B56 regulatory subunit, promotes cell cycle exit by dephosphorylating Cdk2, extending the work to mammalian cells with fluorescent cell cycle sensors and to tumor dormancy in prostate cancer models.

areas.title: Silencing cell cycle genes: chromatin changes during G0
areas.summary: Uses FAIRE-seq, ATAC-seq, and RNA-seq in fruit fly wings to show how nucleosome-mediated silencing and enhancer decommissioning shut down genes such as Cyclin E and cdc25c in prolonged quiescence, with ongoing work on the Brahma and NuRD complexes.

areas.title: Developmental signals that promote quiescence
areas.summary: Examines how the steroid hormone ecdysone triggers cell cycle arrest during metamorphosis, and studies polyploid and variant cell cycles in the Drosophila accessory gland, a prostate-like organ.

areas.title: Cell cycle exit in the aged brain
areas.summary: Investigates abnormal cell cycle re-entry in aging neurons using the fruit fly brain, developing genetic tools to force re-entry and assessing neurodegeneration with behavioral assays.

news.text: Graduate student Hailee Aro completed her Master's defense.
PhD candidate Navyashree Ramesh completed her doctoral defense.
PhD candidate Lizi Yang presented a poster at the FASEB Conference on Cell Cycle Regulation.
Postdoc Deena Damschroder received a GSA travel award for her DROS26 presentation on cell body size changes in the aging Drosophila brain.
Allison Box completed her thesis defense; undergraduate Jingyi Du completed an Honors thesis.
Navyashree Ramesh won 1st place microscopy award at the Midwest Drosophila meeting and 3rd place poster at UM CPOD.
Jaimian Church completed his PhD defense; paper on oncogenic signaling in the Drosophila prostate published.
Three posters presented at the Polyploidy 2023 meeting; ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN protocol paper published in Fly.
